exposure: Maternal risk factors (e.g., gestational diabetes, pre-gestational diabetes, chronic hypertension, preeclampsia, anemia, asthma, obesity, multi parity)
cohort: The study included 1,114 singleton term (>=37 weeks), oligohydramnios (AFI <50 mm) pregnancies from Shamir Medical Center between 2017 and 2021.
finding: High-risk pregnancies with term oligohydramnios were associated with earlier gestational age at delivery, more labor inductions, a higher cesarean section rate, and a higher risk of negative fetal outcomes compared to low-risk pregnancies.
mod_finding: The high-risk group experienced significantly more labor inductions (81% vs 69.7%) and a higher cesarean section rate (19.9% vs 12.4%) compared to the low-risk group.
gest_age: Term (>=37 weeks), with mean gestational age at delivery 39.53 weeks in the high-risk group and 40 weeks in the low-risk group.
